name: web-development
description: Builds and maintains browser front ends - pages, components, styles and their behaviour. Use when a web page or a front-end component is created or changed.

name: react-components
description: Structures React components - props, state, hooks and composition - so they stay small and reusable. Use when a React component is written, split or its state moved between components.

name: react-testing
description: Tests React components through what the user sees, with Testing Library queries, user events and mocked network calls. Use when a component test is written or a flaky one is fixed.

name: css-layout
description: Lays out pages with flexbox and grid, responsive breakpoints and logical spacing instead of fixed offsets. Use when elements overlap, wrap badly or the page breaks on a narrow screen.

name: accessibility-audit
description: Checks a page against WCAG - contrast, keyboard focus order, labels and screen-reader names - and lists each barrier with its fix. Use when a site must be usable without a mouse or with assistive technology.

name: form-validation
description: Validates input in web forms on the client and the server alike, with messages shown beside the field. Use when a form accepts bad data or its errors are unclear to the person filling it in.

name: data-engineering
description: Moves, stores and prepares data for analysis - databases, pipelines and data files. Use when data is loaded, transformed or queried at scale.

name: sql-query-tuning
description: Speeds up a slow SQL query by reading its execution plan, adding or fixing indexes and rewriting joins. Use when a database query takes too long or locks tables.

name: postgres-vacuum
description: Keeps PostgreSQL tables lean - autovacuum settings, table bloat, dead tuples and transaction ID wraparound. Use when a Postgres table grows without new rows or autovacuum falls behind.

name: etl-pipelines
description: Designs extract-transform-load jobs that are idempotent, rerunnable and scheduled, with each stage's input and output recorded. Use when data is copied nightly between systems or a load job fails halfway.

name: data-quality-checks
description: Asserts expectations on datasets - null rates, uniqueness, ranges, referential integrity - and fails the pipeline when they break. Use when reports show impossible numbers or duplicates slip into a table.

name: csv-cleaning
description: Repairs delimited text files - encodings, quoting, inconsistent date formats and broken line ends - before they are imported. Use when an import of a spreadsheet export or a CSV file fails or garbles characters.

name: schema-migrations
description: Changes a database schema through versioned, reversible migration scripts that run without downtime. Use when a column, table or constraint is added, renamed or dropped in a live database.

name: operations
description: Runs services in production - deployment, monitoring, recovery and on-call work. Use when a running service is deployed, observed or restored.

name: incident-response
description: Leads an outage from detection to postmortem - roles, status updates, mitigation first, then a blameless review. Use when users cannot reach a service or an error rate spikes in production.

name: log-analysis
description: Finds the cause of a failure in application and server logs by correlating timestamps, request IDs and error patterns. Use when the only evidence of a problem is in log files or a log search tool.

name: kubernetes-deployments
description: Rolls out workloads on Kubernetes - manifests, readiness probes, resource limits and rolling updates - and rolls them back. Use when pods crash-loop, a rollout stalls or a service is moved onto a cluster.

name: backup-restore
description: Plans backups with retention and offsite copies, and proves them by restoring regularly. Use when data must survive a disk loss or a mistaken deletion, or a restore has never been tried.

name: alert-tuning
description: Turns noisy monitoring alerts into few actionable ones tied to user-facing symptoms and runbooks. Use when on-call engineers are paged too often or ignore alerts.

name: documents
description: Produces office documents and written material - PDFs, spreadsheets, slides and published text. Use when a file meant for people to read or fill in is created or edited.

name: pdf-forms
description: Fills, flattens and extracts fields of PDF forms, and merges or splits PDF files. Use when a PDF has to be filled in programmatically or its pages rearranged.

name: spreadsheet-formulas
description: Writes and debugs spreadsheet formulas - lookups, pivot summaries, conditional sums and date arithmetic - in Excel or Google Sheets. Use when a workbook calculates wrongly or a manual tally should become a formula.

name: slide-decks
description: Builds presentation decks with one message per slide, readable charts and speaker notes. Use when a talk, a pitch or a status review needs slides.

name: release-notes
description: Writes customer-facing release notes that say what changed for the reader and what they must do, grouped by audience. Use when a product version is announced to its users.

name: api-reference-docs
description: Documents an HTTP API endpoint by endpoint - parameters, responses, errors and runnable examples - generated from an OpenAPI description where one exists. Use when an API is published or its documentation is out of date.

name: security
description: Protects systems and data from attack and misuse. Use when work touches credentials, permissions, untrusted input or exposure to the internet.

name: dependency-audit
description: Reviews third-party packages for known vulnerabilities, abandoned maintainers and risky licences, and plans the upgrades. Use when a scanner reports a vulnerable library or a new package is to be added.

name: secret-scanning
description: Finds keys, tokens and passwords committed to repositories or written to logs, and rotates them. Use when a credential may have leaked into source control or a build log.

name: threat-modelling
description: Maps a system's trust boundaries and assets and walks STRIDE over each to find what an attacker could do. Use when a new feature exposes data or an endpoint and its risks are not yet written down.

name: access-review
description: Audits who can do what - accounts, roles, API keys and group memberships - and removes access nobody needs. Use when someone leaves a team or permissions have grown over years.

name: tls-certificates
description: Issues, renews and installs TLS certificates, and diagnoses handshake and chain errors. Use when a site shows a certificate warning or a certificate is about to expire.

name: mobile
description: Builds and ships apps for phones and tablets. Use when an Android or iOS application is developed, built or published.

name: android-builds
description: Fixes Gradle builds of Android apps - dependency conflicts, build variants, R8 shrinking and signing configs. Use when an Android project stops compiling or the release build crashes while the debug build works.

name: ios-signing
description: Sorts out iOS code signing - certificates, provisioning profiles, entitlements and Xcode team settings. Use when Xcode refuses to sign or a build will not install on a device.

name: push-notifications
description: Sends push notifications through APNs and Firebase Cloud Messaging - device tokens, payloads, permission prompts and delivery debugging. Use when users do not receive notifications or a new notification type is added.

name: app-store-release
description: Takes an app through App Store and Google Play review - metadata, screenshots, staged rollout and rejection responses. Use when a mobile version is submitted for review or a submission was rejected.

name: offline-sync
description: Keeps app data usable without a connection - a local store, a change queue and conflict resolution when the device reconnects. Use when an app must work on a train or loses edits made offline.

name: git-commits
description: Writes commit messages and shapes commits so each holds one logical change. Use when changes are committed or a branch's history is cleaned before review.

name: code-review
description: Reviews a change for correctness, readability and design, and words each finding with its consequence and fix. Use when a pull request or a diff is reviewed.

name: debugging
description: Finds the root cause of a defect by reproducing it, narrowing it down and testing one hypothesis at a time. Use when code behaves unexpectedly or a test fails for an unclear reason.

name: unit-testing
description: Writes fast, isolated unit tests - one behaviour each, clear names, no shared state. Use when a function or class gets tests or an existing test is unreliable.

name: refactoring
description: Restructures code without changing what it does, in small steps kept green by tests. Use when code is hard to change, duplicated or tangled.

name: python-style
description: Applies Python conventions - typing, naming, imports, error handling and packaging. Use when Python code is written or reviewed.

name: typescript-style
description: Applies TypeScript conventions - strict types, narrowing, module boundaries and error handling. Use when TypeScript code is written or reviewed.

name: shell-scripts
description: Writes robust shell scripts - quoting, error handling with set -e, portable commands and argument parsing. Use when a Bash or POSIX shell script is written or fixed.

name: docker-images
description: Builds small, reproducible container images - multi-stage Dockerfiles, pinned base images, layer caching and non-root users. Use when a Dockerfile is written or an image is too large or slow to build.

name: ci-pipelines
description: Sets up continuous integration - jobs, caches, test matrices and required checks - in GitHub Actions or GitLab CI. Use when builds should run on every push or a pipeline is slow or flaky.

name: changelog
description: Keeps a CHANGELOG.md in the Keep a Changelog format, one entry per user-visible change. Use when a change is merged or a version is cut.

name: readme-writing
description: Writes a README that says what a project is, how to install and run it, and where to go next. Use when a repository is created or its README is missing or stale.

name: diagramming
description: Draws architecture, sequence and flow diagrams as code with Mermaid or PlantUML. Use when a design needs a picture that lives next to the source.

name: meeting-notes
description: Turns a meeting into notes of decisions, action items with owners and dates, and open questions. Use when a meeting, a call or a transcript is summarised.

name: translation
description: Translates documents, interface strings and emails between languages, keeping terms, tone and formatting. Use when text has to reach readers of another language.

name: regex-help
description: Writes and explains regular expressions, with test strings that match and strings that must not. Use when a pattern has to match, extract or replace text.

name: performance-profiling
description: Profiles CPU and memory use of a program to find the hot path before optimising it, and measures the fix. Use when an application is slow or uses too much memory.

name: project-planning
description: Breaks work into milestones and tasks with estimates, dependencies and risks. Use when a project or a release is scoped and scheduled.

name: email-drafting
description: Drafts clear work emails - one request per message, the ask first, the context after. Use when an email to a colleague, a customer or a vendor is written.

name: release-notes
description: Collects merged pull requests since the last tag into a draft of what a version contains. Use when the changes of a version are gathered from version control.

name: api-design
description: Designs HTTP APIs - resource names, status codes, pagination, versioning and error bodies. Use when a new endpoint or a breaking change to an API is planned.

name: dependency-updates
description: Updates a project's dependencies in batches, reading changelogs for breaking changes and running the tests after each. Use when packages are outdated or an update bot opens pull requests.

name: linux-admin
description: Administers Linux servers - users, services with systemd, disks, firewall rules and package updates. Use when a server is configured or a service on it does not start.
